article_exact_sense_rule.criterion: English meaning matches the dictionary sense after punctuation/case normalization, and each candidate article is present in the existing German noun-gender index.

reviewed_examples.german: Wir brauchen nicht viel Platz.
reviewed_examples.english: We don't require much space.
reviewed_examples.note: The example uses brauchen in the sense require.

reviewed_examples.german: Tom hörte für einen Moment auf zu lesen.
reviewed_examples.english: Tom stopped reading for a moment.
reviewed_examples.note: Moment is used with its time-interval meaning.

reviewed_examples.german: Der Junge hat eine Uhr in der Hand.
reviewed_examples.english: The boy has a watch in his hand.

reviewed_examples.german: Da ist ein Herr, der dich sehen will.
reviewed_examples.english: There is a gentleman to see you.

reviewed_examples.german: Darf ich fragen, wie du heißt?
reviewed_examples.english: May I have your name, please?
reviewed_examples.note: heißen is used to ask a person's name.

reviewed_examples.german: Mein Rat an Sie ist, sofort zu gehen.
reviewed_examples.english: My advice to you is to leave immediately.

reviewed_examples.german: Mein Sohn ist jetzt so groß wie ich.
reviewed_examples.english: My son is now as tall as I am.

reviewed_examples.german: Ich bin lieber für mich allein.
reviewed_examples.english: I prefer my own company.

reviewed_examples.german: Wir wissen beide, dass es zu spät ist.
reviewed_examples.english: We both know it's too late.

reviewed_examples.german: Geben Sie mir bitte von jeder Sorte drei.
reviewed_examples.english: Please give me three of each kind.

reviewed_examples.german: Ich nehme an, der Junge, der dir so ähnlich sieht, ist dein Bruder.
reviewed_examples.english: I assume that boy who looks so much like you is your brother.

reviewed_examples.german: Vielen Dank für alles, was ihr getan habt!
reviewed_examples.english: Thanks a lot for everything you've done.

reviewed_examples.german: Ich habe immer noch meine Würde.
reviewed_examples.english: I still have my dignity.

reviewed_examples.german: Der Baum stand kurz vor dem Fall.
reviewed_examples.english: The tree was ready to fall down.
reviewed_examples.note: Fall means a falling event here.

reviewed_examples.german: Mein Kuli ist nicht so gut wie deiner.
reviewed_examples.english: My pen isn't as good as yours.
reviewed_examples.note: deiner is used as a possessive pronoun.

reviewed_examples.german: Das Buch kennen alle kleinen Kinder.
reviewed_examples.english: That book is familiar to all young children.

reviewed_examples.german: Er hat eine Frage zum Abendessen an Sie, Herr.
reviewed_examples.english: He has a question for you regarding dinner, sir.

reviewed_examples.german: Um wie viel Uhr esst ihr zu Abend?
reviewed_examples.english: What time do you have dinner?

reviewed_examples.german: Es gibt viele hohe Häuser in dieser Stadt.
reviewed_examples.english: The town has many tall buildings.
reviewed_examples.note: Selected this alternative because it better illustrates Stadt than the other candidate.

reviewed_examples.german: Bald schlief das Baby in der Wiege ein.
reviewed_examples.english: The baby soon fell asleep in the cradle.

reviewed_examples.german: Er hörte nicht, dass sein Name gerufen wurde.
reviewed_examples.english: He didn't hear his name called.

reviewed_examples.german: Es hatte den Kopf einer Frau, den Körper eines Löwen, die Flügel eines Vogels und den Schwanz einer Schlange.
reviewed_examples.english: It had the head of a woman, the body of a lion, the wings of a bird, and the tail of a serpent.

reviewed_examples.german: Ich trage lieber ein T-Shirt, das zu groß ist, als eines, das zu klein ist.
reviewed_examples.english: I'd rather wear a T-shirt that's too large than one that's too small.
reviewed_examples.note: Selected this alternative because it directly uses klein to mean small.

reviewed_examples.german: Tom wachte etwas später auf als ich.
reviewed_examples.english: Tom woke up a little after I did.

reviewed_examples.german: Ich habe ein paar Freunde in den USA.
reviewed_examples.english: I have a few friends in the United States.

reviewed_examples.german: Du musst bis zum Ende des Monats mit dieser Arbeit fertig sein.
reviewed_examples.english: You are to finish this work by the end of this month.

reviewed_examples.german: Könnte ich eine Minute deiner Zeit haben?
reviewed_examples.english: Could I have a minute of your time?
reviewed_examples.note: Minute means a unit of time.

reviewed_examples.german: Ich bin bereit, alles für dich zu tun.
reviewed_examples.english: I'm ready to do anything for you.

reviewed_examples.german: Er machte seinen Mund weit auf.
reviewed_examples.english: He opened his mouth wide.

reviewed_examples.german: Tom hatte nur eine leise Ahnung davon, was Mary meinte.
reviewed_examples.english: Tom only had a faint inkling of what Mary was talking about.

reviewed_examples.german: Du musst ziehen, um die Tür zu öffnen.
reviewed_examples.english: You need to pull that door to open it.

reviewed_examples.german: Ein Auto hat vier Räder.
reviewed_examples.english: An automobile has four wheels.

reviewed_examples.german: Sie hielt ihr Baby in den Armen.
reviewed_examples.english: She held her baby in her arms.
reviewed_examples.note: The context identifies Armen as dative plural of Arm, the body part; this corrected the prior homograph mapping.

reviewed_examples.german: Ich werde es in Betracht ziehen.
reviewed_examples.english: I'll take that into consideration.
reviewed_examples.note: This illustrates the fixed expression in Betracht ziehen.

reviewed_examples.german: Das Kind schlief auf dem Schoß seiner Mutter.
reviewed_examples.english: The child slept on its mother's lap.

held_examples.reason: The supplied example uses the verbal participle of finden, while the entry is tagged adjective; no adjective-sense candidate was confirmed.
The supplied examples use the idiom Händchen halten and do not match the entry gloss about holding an object.
Available examples use fixed phrases and do not clearly illustrate the current standalone English gloss.

Biest.note: Duden confirms das Biest and the plural Biester for the animal/figurative sense.

Lake.note: Duden confirms feminine Lake and plural Laken for brine.

Diner.meaning: diner; small restaurant, especially in the United States
Diner.note: Correct the candidate das to der for the restaurant sense; Duden distinguishes the neuter meal sense.

Schoß.note: Duden confirms masculine Schoß for the lap/body-part sense and plural Schöße.

Armen.article_note: Inflected dative plural of the noun der Arm (body part); its nominative plural is die Arme. The surface form Armen appears after den, as in in den Armen.
Armen.plural_note: Inflected form: dative plural of der Arm; nominative plural die Arme, dative plural den Armen.
Armen.meaning: arms (dative plural of Arm, the body part)
Armen.form_note: Dative plural of Arm (body part); example usage: in den Armen.
Armen.note: The original candidate described forms of Armer, but the bilingual example uses the noun Arm. Keep Armen as a frequency surface form and link it to Arm.

Betracht.article_note: Used in fixed expressions such as in Betracht ziehen and außer Betracht lassen; no standalone article is used in these constructions.
Betracht.plural_note: Usually singular; occurs mainly in fixed expressions such as in Betracht ziehen and außer Betracht lassen.
Betracht.note: Duden records fixed expressions rather than an independent article-bearing use.
